notes:
CISA is the US government agency responsible for protecting critical infrastructure from cyber threats, created in 2018 replacing NPPD (National Protection and Programs Directorate). CISA has operational authority over US federal cybersecurity: it coordinates vulnerability disclosure, issues Binding Operational Directives (BODs) and Emergency Directives (EDs), contracts MITRE to operate the CVE Program, and maintains the KEV catalog and Vulnrichment project.

CISA also handles ICS-CERT advisories for industrial control systems. The two sources registered here — KEV and Vulnrichment — serve different purposes: KEV is a prioritization signal (confirmed exploitation), while Vulnrichment provides CVE enrichment data (CWE, CVSS, CPE) to address NVD's processing backlog.

data.description: CISA's authoritative catalog of vulnerabilities confirmed to be actively exploited in the wild. Federal agencies are required to remediate KEV entries within specified timeframes under BOD 22-01.
data.notes:
KEV is a prioritization signal, not just another vulnerability list. Every entry has evidence of active exploitation. BOD 22-01 requires federal agencies to remediate KEV entries, and many non-federal organizations also use KEV status as a prioritization factor. The catalog contains roughly 1,200 entries compared to 200,000+ total CVEs — only confirmed exploited vulnerabilities are included.

KEV entries reference CVE IDs as identifiers, so the SecID subpath uses the CVE ID format. JSON and CSV feeds are updated as new vulnerabilities are added. Due dates are included for federal agency compliance tracking.

examples.note: Log4Shell — one of the first CVEs added to KEV

data.description: CISA's CVE enrichment initiative providing additional context for CVE records including CWE mappings, CVSS scores, and CPE data to address NVD's enrichment backlog.
data.notes:
Vulnrichment provides faster enrichment than waiting for NVD processing. Enrichment data follows CVE JSON 5.x format and is contributed back to the CVE ecosystem. The GitHub repository organizes enriched CVE records by year and bucket directories at the repository root ({year}/{bucket}/{id}.json), matching the cvelistV5 bucket convention.

The lookup URL requires extracting both the 4-digit year and the bucket prefix from the CVE ID to construct the correct GitHub path.

urls.auth: Public GitHub repo, no auth for clone/download. Use token for higher rate limits.
urls.notes: One CVE JSON 5.x file per CVE at {year}/{bucket}/{id}.json on the develop branch.
